description.short_caption: Endoscopic view of a rectal mass with irregular surface before biopsy.
description.detailed_description: This endoscopic image shows the rectal lumen with a prominent mass. The mass has an irregular, nodular surface with areas of erythema and possible ulceration. Surrounding mucosa appears relatively normal. The image is taken prior to biopsy, and the mass occupies a significant portion of the lumen.
visible_findings: irregular, nodular mass in the rectum
areas of erythema and possible ulceration

description.short_caption: Endoscopic view of rectal mucosa with nodular lesions post-biopsy.
description.detailed_description: This endoscopic image shows the rectal mucosa with multiple raised, nodular lesions. The mucosa appears erythematous and inflamed, with some areas of irregularity and possible biopsy sites. The nodules are prominent and distributed across the visible mucosal surface. There is evidence of mild bleeding, likely related to recent biopsy procedures.

description.short_caption: GMS stain showing a fungal organism with a thick capsule.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stain of a tissue biopsy. A single fungal organism is visible, characterized by a thick, darkly stained capsule and a lighter interior. The background tissue is stained light blue-green, providing contrast to the organism. The morphology is consistent with a yeast form, possibly Cryptococcus species, given the prominent capsule.
visible_findings: fungal organism with a thick capsule
dark staining of the capsule with GMS

description.short_caption: MRI of the abdomen showing a cystic lesion with surrounding bowel loops.
description.detailed_description: This is a coronal MRI image of the abdomen. A large, well-defined cystic lesion is visible in the lower abdomen, labeled 'A'. Surrounding bowel loops are noted, with some appearing distended, labeled 'B'. The lesion appears to have a homogenous fluid signal, consistent with a cystic structure. No obvious signs of solid components or septations are visible. The image is de-identified and suitable for educational purposes.
visible_findings: large cystic lesion in the lower abdomen
homogenous fluid signal within the lesion

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing parasitic structure in tissue, H&E stain.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image, stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), shows a cross-section of tissue containing a large, elongated parasitic structure with a thick, eosinophilic outer layer and internal structures. Surrounding the parasite are numerous inflammatory cells, predominantly lymphocytes and eosinophils, indicating a host immune response. The parasite appears to be embedded within the tissue, suggesting an active infection.
visible_findings: thick eosinophilic outer layer of the parasite
surrounding inflammatory cells, including lymphocytes and eosinophils
